records.title: Mitigating Forward Model Mismatch in Inverse Problems via Learned Residuals and Diffusion Priors
records.version: Complete publisher-formatted SPIE article, volume 14016, article 140160D, 12 pages, 2026 imprint; conference name SPIE ABC 2025.
records.read_extent: Main text pp. 1-8, sections 1-4, equations 1-11 and figures 1-5 inspected. Pages 4-8 rendered and visually inspected. References pp. 8-12 scanned, not independently audited. No supplement/code supplied.
records.source_kind: User-supplied PDF; user reports receipt from Professor Jang. Canonical DOI is bibliographic provenance, not a claim of remote PDF retrieval.
records.technical: A diffusion prior and regularised shallow residual network jointly reconstruct x and additive measurement discrepancy r; a second diffusion pass refines x. Reported DHM tests use propagation-distance mismatch; the scattering experiment is explicitly simulated and absorbs outside-memory-effect contributions into r. Section 3.3 defines zeta as true-versus-perturbed model discrepancy normalised by measurement norm and identifies an empirical visual failure threshold near 0.1. No evaluated image/operator uncertainty or calibrated selective risk is demonstrated.
records.feature_locator: O/P/Q: sections 2.3-2.4, equation 8, figure 1, pp. 4-5; R/X: section 3.3, equation 11, figure 5, pp. 7-8; S/T/U/V: sections 3.1-3.3, figures 2-5, pp. 5-8; W: sections 2.4, 3.2-3.3 and figures 2-5.
records.applicability: O=Partial: image and nuisance discrepancy, not physical operator inference. P=No: diffusion reconstruction trajectories are not an evaluated uncertainty output. Q/R=No: no physical-parameter distribution or probability calibration. S=Partial: deliberate physical/model shifts, incomplete training/test separation detail. T=Yes for reported DHM measurements only; scattering is simulated. U/V=No under compound-process/video definitions. W=Partial for visual artifact comparisons and signal-absorption analysis, not a hallucination detector. X=Partial because the dictionary includes explicit reliability thresholds; zeta is an empirical failure boundary, not a deployable calibrated reject/patch-selection rule.

3.evidence: Explicit forward-model discrepancy correction, image/residual identifiability and empirical operational-boundary analysis (sections 2.3-3.3).

4.evidence: Primary technical method with equations, algorithm schematic, comparison images and mismatch sweeps (figures 1-5).

quality_followups: Exact reproduction requires residual-network architecture, hyperparameters, checkpoints, data counts, source-disjoint splits, code and runtime. No code link is printed in the supplied PDF; public availability not exhaustively searched.
Clarify reference-phase construction and calibration/test independence. Visual fidelity examples do not establish calibrated selected-detail reliability.

Equation 11 uses true and perturbed physical parameters and a common object; an estimator available from unknown captures alone is not demonstrated. A learned-residual norm is a proxy, not the same quantity.
Figure 5b appears nonzero at zero depth mismatch, whereas equation 11 is zero for coincident model evaluations. Clarify the plotted definition; do not infer a noise-floor explanation.
Abstract/introduction imply real-world scattering but section 3.2 explicitly uses simulation. Code hardware evidence only for the reported DHM demonstration.
Equation 8 uses a signal-shaped residual; section 2.3 initially writes an error magnitude. Do not conflate these in implementation.
